title: Investigation Playbook: Inference Cost Anomalies
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for triaging and resolving unexpected cost anomalies in inference usage. Focus is on operational signals we can check quickly (within 15–60 minutes) and a set of longer-term follow-ups to prevent recurrence. This doc is written for on-call operators, SREs, and product owners when alerted by cost-aggregation or billing anomalies (e.g. daily committed spend > expected, token-unit spikes, GPU hours surge).

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies to hosted Redwood API and Dedicated pools. Private deployments may reuse steps but with different telemetry endpoints.
- Anomalies covered: sudden sustained increase in per-token cost, GPU-hour overrun, unexpected egress or billing tags, and anomalous hosted-model routing that increases expensive variants.
- Not covered: manual invoice disputes or cloud provider billing reconciliation.

Triage goals (ordered):
1) Confirm the anomaly is real (billing pipeline vs. telemetry mismatch).
2) Rapidly isolate likely root cause class (traffic spike, model change, config drift, KV cache cold, misrouting, billing tag mis-attr).
3) Apply safe mitigations (rate-limits, fallback to cheaper model variant, pause feature flag).
4) Postmortem and action items assigned.

Primary signals and where to check them (quick checklist):
- Cost aggregate dashboard (team: billing): check date window, compare token-units, embeddings-units, GPU-hours.
- Token throughput and P50/P95 latency panels (observability; inference-tokenflow).
- Model routing histogram: percent traffic to each model variant (per-customer and global).
- KV cache hit ratio and prefix-warmth per tenant.
- Batch size distribution and average per-model.
- Autoscaling events & instance churn: look for repeated scaling / OOMs.
- Ingestion of bulk jobs (one-off jobs): check job-run logs and scheduled tasks.
- Billing tags / usage metadata: untagged traffic or new service accounts.

Concrete metric definitions (quick reference):
- token_units_total (sum, per-hour): count of generated tokens counted by billing pipeline.
- embedding_units_total (sum, per-hour): embedding calls counted.
- gpu_hours_consumed (sum, per-hour): reported GPU runtime consumed by Dedicated pools.
- kvcache_hit_ratio (ratio, 5m): kv_cache_hits / (kv_cache_hits + kv_cache_misses).
- model_variant_pct (distribution): percent of total requests routed to variant X.
- avg_batch_size (avg, 1m): average model micro-batch size in serving runtime.
- per_request_duration_ms (p50/p95/p99): end-to-end inference duration per request.
- request_retries_total (sum): retries due to failures or fallback policies.

Anchors for tracing and span lookups:
- Span name: inference.request -> attributes: model_variant, tenant_id, request_route, batch_size, kv_cache_status
- Trace labels: billing_tag, commit_sha, deployment_region, container_id
- Trace sampling: for cost anomalies increase sampling to 100% for affected tenants/model routes for 1 hour (use sampling override flag).

Investigation flow (first 15 min):
1) Confirm billing vs telemetry: compare billing-dashboard token_units_total to realtime token ingestion pipeline (streaming telemetry). If mismatch > 5–10%, tag as \"billing pipeline discrepancy\" and escalate to billing pipeline owners.
2) Look for sudden traffic source: filter requests by tenant, route, and auth key. Run panel filter: tenant_id = high-cost-tenant OR auth_key = new_key
3) Check model routing: is there a surge of traffic to an expensive variant? If model_variant_pct shows shift > 15% in last 30m, note model rollout PR/feature flag.
4) KV cache: inspect kvcache_hit_ratio over last 24h and prefix-level warmth for top affected tenants. Cold caches increase tokens generated (more prefix + kv misses) and can spike GPU time.
5) Batch size & autoscaling: small batch sizes and high request rate can multiply per-token overhead. Check avg_batch_size and recent autoscale events; a flapping pool can cause inefficient GPU utilization.
6) Scheduled bulk jobs: search for job-run logs (job-run-*), ingestion API calls from CI/service accounts, or big import endpoints.
7) Confirm whether a model weights update or quantization change was deployed in the window. Check commit_shas tied to traces and deployment dashboard.

Quick mitigations (choose safest first):
- If model routing caused it: rollback to previous routing config or pin global fallback to cheaper variant.
- If single tenant: throttle that tenant’s rate-limit (apply temporary quota).
- If KV cache cold: enable prefix-warmup for affected tenant (if available) and schedule a manual warmup run (small synthetic requests).
- If autoscaling churn: temporarily increase minimum pool size, or disable aggressive scale-down for the impacted pool.
- If bulk job: pause/cancel job if non-critical.
- If billing tag mis-attr: re-tag usage when possible and notify finance; but mitigate root traffic source.

Example diagnostic queries / snippets (pseudo-SQL / PromQL style):
- Find top tenants by token_units in last 2h: SELECT tenant_id, SUM(token_units) FROM billing_events WHERE timestamp > now() - 2h GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY SUM(token_units) DESC LIMIT 50
- Check model routing change vector: SELECT model_variant, COUNT(*) FROM inference_requests WHERE timestamp > now() - 30m GROUP BY model_variant ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
- KV cache hit ratio by tenant: promql: sum(kv_cache_hits{tenant=~\"$tenant\"}) / sum(kv_cache_hits{tenant=~\"$tenant\"} + kv_cache_misses{tenant=~\"$tenant\"})
- GPU hours by pool: SELECT pool_id, SUM(gpu_seconds) / 3600 FROM runtime_usage WHERE ts > now() - 24h GROUP BY pool_id

Severity definitions (cost-focused):
- Sev 1 (critical): daily projected spend increases > 50% vs baseline and billing exposure > $10k in 24h without mitigation. Requires immediate action and incident response.
- Sev 2 (high): projected spend increase 20–50% or sustained expensive GPU-hour surge localized to one cluster. Escalate to SRE lead.
- Sev 3 (medium): anomalous variance < 20% or single-tenant spike under thresholds. Handle via operator mitigations and follow-up.

Post-incident tasks (owner assignment checklist):
- Create a running incident timeline (who did what, times) and attach key graphs and traces.
- If caused by config/PR: link PR, rollback notes, and schedule a rollout guard (feature flag, incremental canary).
- If caused by tenant workload: contact customer-success and propose rate-limit/quota adjustments or cost-saving recommendations.
- Instrumentation gaps: add aggregation metrics where we lacked visibility (e.g., per-route batch_size histogram, per-tenant kv prefix warmth).
- Cost guard rails: propose quota alerts and automated slow-fail fallback to cheaper models when cross-day spend exceeds X% of baseline.

Dashboard and widget checklist to add/verify (short-term priorities):
- Top-N tenants by token and GPU-hour with a heatmap over last 48h.
- Model-variant routing delta widget with timeframe compare (30m vs 24h).
- KV cache heatmap by tenant with prefix warmth trendline.
- Autoscale churn tracker (scale events per hour) and GPU utilization distribution.
- Daily projected spend panel with rolling window and alerting threshold (configurable).

Longer-term mitigations & product changes (backlog candidates):
- Per-tenant prewarming API and automated warmup triggers after deploys/rollouts.
- Cost-aware routing: automatic fallback to quantized/cheaper variants when per-tenant spend crosses policies.
- Batching advisor: runtime recommendations surfaced in Console per route, with cost delta estimates.
- Billing reconciliation automation: cross-check streaming telemetry and invoice data nightly and auto-raise tickets on >5% delta.

Notes, TODOs, known limitations (working):
- Current billing tags are not consistently propagated for some internal service accounts (TODO: pipeline fix, JIRA-4821).
- We do not yet capture per-request kv prefix id consistently — adding this is in backlog.
- Synthetic warmups are coarse today; need targeted prefix-level warmups.

Owners & rotation:
- Primary investigator (on-call): eng-observability oncall (pager duty).
- Billing pipeline owner: finance-infra squad.
- Follow-up PM: product-hosted-api.

If you are the on-call and need help: escalate to Samir Gupta (pager), or ping #eng-observability with subject \"cost-anomaly <tenant|global>\". Attach top 3 graphs and a sample trace id.

Appendix: quick checklist for finalizing postmortem
- Root cause labeled and confidence (low/medium/high).
- Impact table (tenants affected, estimated cost delta, duration).
- Mitigations executed with timestamps.
- Action items with owners and due dates.

End of draft playbook.

Revision notes: 2024-11-07 added severity thresholds and runbook query snippets; 2024-02-20 initial draft.
